title: Signed data pioneer SignSplit launches with $400M to help everyone get paid for their AI contributions
source_used: SiliconANGLE (the pool item, read in full) and the company's press release on PR Newswire dated 5 Oct 2026.
key_facts: SignSplit PBC, founded in 2024 and incorporated as a Delaware public benefit corporation, announced on 5 Oct 2026 a $400 million 'strategic seed round' with W Group at a $1 billion valuation (company release; SiliconANGLE).
The release says the financing 'combines capital with a multi-year package of strategic resources to support SignSplit's global rollout'.

W Group is a group of 11 businesses (SiliconANGLE: financial technology firms focused on blockchain); its founder and president Volodymyr Nosov says the group will put additional capital and resources behind a rapid global rollout.
SignSplit's 'signed data' means human data contributions with established provenance and clear consent for use under defined terms.

Individuals can sign their data, voice, likeness or other work, or place data in 'data pools' for AI developers and are paid according to how often it is used; businesses can create their own pools, and 'research pools' serve universities and life sciences firms.
A verification layer lets organizations check whether a dataset or likeness is signed.
Alessandro Monterosso is co-founder and chief executive; no AI developer or other customer is named in the article or in the release.
quote_evidence: Signed data refers to human data contributions that have established provenance and give clear consent for it to be used under defined terms.
The financing commitment, which values SignSplit at $1 billion, combines capital with a multi-year package of strategic resources to support SignSplit's global rollout.
For individual contributors, SignSplit offers a clear promise: They simply “sign the data and split the value.”
why_it_matters_hint: A newly launched company offers a way to attach consent and payment to personal data used for AI, backed by a large first round.
notes: The company's own release (PR Newswire, 5 Oct 2026) is the primary source; SiliconANGLE wrote its own account of it. The amount and valuation are the company's own figures, and the release says the round combines capital with a package of strategic resources, so not all of it need be cash. SiliconANGLE spells the name inconsistently (SignSplit, SplitSign, SignedSplit); 'SignSplit' is used as in the release.
